components.note: Durrett Step 1 (p. 18): the representation-independence remark is proved; Durrett's signed simple functions on finite-measure pieces are bridged in annex lines 244-246; zero-times-infinity boundary stated.
Durrett Lemma 1.4.1 (p. 19) by common refinement; the a.e. and absolute-value parts (Lemma 1.4.2) are covered by the signed theory.
Durrett Step 3 (p. 21) and the a.e. notion (p. 18); the different supremum definition is identified with Durrett's in thm:p15-integral-source-bridge.

components.gap: Durrett's Exercises 1.5.5 (p. 28) and 1.6.13 (p. 37) replace the nonnegativity hypothesis of monotone convergence by integrability of the first negative part: if g_n increases to g and the integral of g_1^- is finite then the integrals of g_n increase to that of g; if E X_1^- < infinity and X_n increases to X then E X_n increases to E X. This hypothesis variant is not stated in the theorem (lines 81-90) or anywhere on the input route; lines 260-262 show only that monotonicity alone does not suffice. Its only rendering is in uninserted w02c files.
source_locators: Durrett Thm 1.5.7 p. 27; Exercises 1.5.5 p. 28, 1.6.13 p. 37

components.gap: Durrett's Exercise 1.5.10 (p. 28) gives the signed series interchange: if the sum over n of the integrals of |f_n| is finite then sum_n of the integrals of f_n equals the integral of sum_n f_n. The theorem (lines 92-116) states the series formula only for nonnegative f_n (covering Exercises 1.4.1, 1.5.4, 1.5.6, 1.6.15, Lemma 1.4.5 and Fatou, Thm 1.5.5); the absolutely summable signed variant is not supplied on the input route.
source_locators: Durrett Lemma 1.4.5 p. 22, Thm 1.5.5 p. 26, Exercises 1.5.4, 1.5.6, 1.5.10 p. 28

components.gap: Durrett fixes notation for special cases of the integral (pp. 23-24): the integral of f(x)dx for Lebesgue measure on R^d; the integral from a to b of f(x)dx for the integral over [a,b] against Lebesgue measure; the integral of f(x)dG(x) for the measure with mass G(b)-G(a) on (a,b]; and sum_i f(i) for counting measure on a countable set, 'to indicate that results for sums follow from those for integrals'. Neither this definition nor the chapter introduces these notations or the counting-measure reading of sums, although later chapters write integrals as f(x,y)dx.
source_locators: Durrett Step 4 and 'Notation for special cases', pp. 22-24

components.gap: The bridge identifies the constructions with Durrett's Steps 1-4 and proves Step 2 (sup = inf) and Lemma 1.4.4. Not supplied: Durrett's statement that the four-step sequence (simple, bounded, nonnegative, general functions) 'is also useful in proving integration formulas' (p. 18, citing the proofs of Thms 1.6.9 and 1.7.2), the method he names when proving Thm 1.6.9 ('The reader should note the method employed, since it will be used several times below', p. 32). No on-route item states this proof procedure.
source_locators: Durrett pp. 18-21 Steps 1-3, Lemma 1.4.4; p. 32 proof of Thm 1.6.9

components.gap: Durrett's definition of convergence in measure (p. 26) carries the claim that on a space of finite measure it is a weaker assumption than convergence a.e. (a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure when the total measure is finite). The definition (lines 197-217) neither states nor proves this; the input route has only the probability-space case, in a later chapter this entry does not reference (limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex lines 194-202).

components.note: Durrett Thms 1.5.3 and 1.5.8 (pp. 26-27) and 1.6.7 with the bounded-convergence naming (p. 30); hypotheses weakened to a.e. and conclusions strengthened to L1.
Durrett Examples 1.5.4 (p. 26) and 1.5.6 (p. 27) with added no-dominator, signed-Fatou and monotone-signed boundaries; computations verified.
Durrett Thm 1.5.2 (p. 25), Thm 1.6.3 with endpoints p,q in [1,infinity] (p. 29) and the Cauchy-Schwarz case (p. 26), zero and infinite norms included.
Durrett's convexity definition (p. 25, p. 29); supporting line and continuity proved without differentiability.

components.gap: Durrett Thm 1.5.1/1.6.2 itself is covered (its special cases |EX| <= E|X| and (EX)^2 <= E X^2 are on the route via thm:p15-signed-integral-laws and thm:p15-expectation-bounds). Not supplied: Exercise 1.6.1 (p. 35), the equality case for strictly convex phi (phi(EX) = E phi(X) forces X = EX a.s.), and Exercise 1.6.2 (p. 35), the multivariate inequality E phi(X1,...,Xn) >= phi(EX1,...,EXn) for convex phi on R^n with the stated integrability; nor the arithmetic-geometric mean consequence of Exercise 1.6.12 (p. 37). None of these is on the input route.
source_locators: Durrett Thm 1.6.2 p. 29; Exercises 1.6.1, 1.6.2 p. 35, 1.6.12 p. 37

components.note: Durrett sec. 1.6 definitions (pp. 28-29, 33): existence convention, mean, E(X;A), k-th moment, variance.

components.gap: The identity of Durrett Thm 1.6.9 and Thm 1.6.1 are proved (including the nonnegative infinite-mean affine branch). Not supplied: the theorem's name 'change of variables formula', its notation (the integral over S of f(y) mu(dy)), and Durrett's remark explaining the name (writing h for X and P o h^{-1} for the law, the integral of f(h(w))dP equals the integral of f(y) d(P o h^{-1})) (p. 32); the motive that computations must shift to a space on which one can do calculus (p. 32); and the stated consequence that expected values of functions of random variables are computed by integrals on the real line (p. 33). No on-route item gives them.
source_locators: Durrett Thm 1.6.1 p. 29; Thm 1.6.9 and remarks pp. 32-33

components.gap: Durrett Thm 1.6.4 with its naming remark and (1.6.2)-(1.6.4) are covered. Not supplied: Exercise 1.6.3 (p. 35), that Chebyshev's inequality is sharp (for 0 < b <= a some X has E X^2 = b^2 and P(|X| >= a) = b^2/a^2) and not sharp (a^2 P(|X| >= a)/E X^2 -> 0 when 0 < E X^2 < infinity); Exercise 1.6.4 (p. 36), the one-sided bound via phi(x) = (x+b)^2 with its two-point extremal law and P(Y >= a) <= sigma^2/(a^2+sigma^2); and Exercise 1.6.5 (p. 36), the two nonexistent lower bounds. Only an averaged one-sided Chebyshev statement appears on the route, unreferenced (variance-and-dependent-concentration.tex lines 298-315).

components.note: Handbook example; the uniform simple-function bounds, limits and Var(U) = 1/12 are proved with written steps, and the undefined signed mean is verified.

components.gap: Durrett Thm 1.6.8 (p. 31) and its p > 1 special case are covered with full proof. Not supplied: Exercise 1.6.7 (p. 36), which shows the theorem reaches beyond domination: on (0,1) with alpha in (1,2), X_n = n^alpha 1_(1/(n+1),1/n) tends to 0 a.s., the theorem applies with h(x) = x and g(x) = |x|^(2/alpha), yet no integrable function dominates the X_n. The handbook's no-dominator example (lines 237-251) concerns f_n with integral one, to which Thm 1.6.8 does not apply.
